name: Orinola Szczepańska-Tuivaga
role: Laundry operator and alterations service owner
location: Hamtramck Enclave, Wash-Block 7 (a row of steam-vented stalls near the Enclave's main pedestrian artery), near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Orinola is a broad-shouldered woman whose arms are ropey with muscle from decades of wringing, hauling, and pressing. Her skin is deep brown and perpetually damp at the temples, and she wears her silver-streaked hair pinned back under a waxed canvas cap. She has no dramatic augmentations — just a single subdermal temp-sensor strip along her left forearm so she always knows the water temperature without testing it by hand, a practical choice made thirty years ago and never regretted. Her face is a map of practical expressions: skeptical squint, satisfied nod, the slow blink she uses when someone is wasting her time.

She runs Szczepańska's Wash & Mend out of a narrow storefront that smells of lye, eucalyptus pressing compound, and the faint burnt-sugar scent of the seam-welder she uses for alterations. She knows every household in a four-block radius by the state of their laundry. She can tell you who is sick (strange smell, unwashed for two weeks), who just got lucky (dress shirts pressed three days in a row), and who is grieving (everything black, brought in without a word). She is not a gossip — she is a reader. There is a difference, and she will explain it to you firmly if you confuse the two.

core_fears: Her shop being seized by a corponation redevelopment zone
Outliving her usefulness to people who depend on her
core_desires: To be genuinely irreplaceable to her community
To one day retire without the community collapsing behind her
coping_mechanisms: Throws herself into physical work when anxious
Prays to Sudsa the boiler-E.L.F. in long, practical monologues
blind_spots: Underestimates how much people actually like her — assumes all goodwill is transactional
Refuses to acknowledge her shop's finances are deteriorating
psychology.secret: She has been quietly subsidizing two families in the Enclave whose breadwinners died — laundering their clothes for free for over a year and telling them the machines are 'running a special.' She keeps a second set of books so no one discovers her charity.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Direct, practical Creole-inflected cadence with occasional Polish phrases absorbed from the neighborhood. Uses laundry and textile metaphors constantly without noticing.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried; she never rushes a sentence any more than she rushes a rinse cycle
verbal_tics: 'That's how it comes out in the wash.'
Clicks her tongue before delivering bad news
example_lines: 'Bring it before the smell sets, yes? After that, I am miracle-worker, not magician.'
'You want to know about the Ferreiras? Look at their sheets. That tells you everything a conversation won't.'

story_hooks: A jacket came in with a sealed inner pocket she has never seen before — the owner hasn't returned for it in six weeks

The Enclave Small Operators Collective is being pressured to accept a Tessera 'partnership' deal that would effectively turn all their storefronts into franchise nodes — Orinola is the holdout and she needs allies
narrative_function: Neighborhood oracle and information sieve — she knows everyone's business through their laundry and will share carefully selected observations with people she trusts. Quest giver for domestic disputes, missing persons in the Enclave, or anything that arrives in someone's pockets and shouldn't have.
augmentations: Subdermal temperature-sensing strip along left forearm (utilitarian, faded blue indicator light). No cosmetic mods.
daily_life: She opens the wash-block at 05:30, running the first loads before the Enclave's water-pressure peak, then handles alterations and mending in the afternoon lull. She closes at 21:00 and leaves data offerings at the small E.L.F. shrine built into her boiler unit — a deity she calls Sudsa, whom she credits with keeping her ancient machines running.
affiliation: Independent; loose member of the Hamtramck Enclave Small Operators Collective

decision_rules: Never share information that would directly harm a client — share only what protects
Always finish the job before starting an argument
escalation_ladder: The long silence and the slow blink
Explicit statement of consequences in a very quiet voice

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses them through practical questions — what do they need, what do they have, are they going to be trouble
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm but still measures everything; expresses affection through doing, not saying

stress_responses.low: Works faster and hums to herself
stress_responses.high: Sends everyone out of the shop and talks to Sudsa for twenty minutes alone

contradictions: Insists she is not sentimental, but has kept every handwritten thank-you note she has ever received in a box under the counter
habits: Wipes her hands on her apron between every task even when they are already dry
Checks the boiler-shrine every morning with a small offering of clean water
breaking_points: Watching someone exploit a neighbor who trusted them — she will intervene regardless of personal cost

timeline.event: Born in Hamtramck Enclave to a Polish-Fijian household
Took over the wash-block from her aunt after a ferrogate accident left the older woman unable to stand for long hours
Survived a Tessera rezoning attempt that cleared four neighboring shops; her collective action was the first organized resistance in the Enclave in a decade
